background: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a 2048x2048 raster art master containing FOUR SEPARATE square watercolor textbook background panels in an exact 2 columns by 2 rows grid, no gutters and no borders. Each square is 1024x1024. Input reference is ONLY a style reference: reproduce its translucent coral, lavender, pale ochre, indigo fine hand pen, watercolor blooms, warm textured paper and graceful confident handwriting. Modern clear hierarchy for grades 9–10, deliberately enlarged anatomical mechanisms, not an antique chart. Each panel's LOWER HALF MUST BE EMPTY warm paper, because game objects will occupy it. All anatomy and annotation contained in TOP HALF only. TOP LEFT: heading "An inside of its own", a small animal-cell locator left and a very large phospholipid double layer right showing blue round heads facing water above and below, paired golden tails inward. Three tiny labels only: "water", "heads", "tails". Do not paint a completed draggable cell. TOP RIGHT: heading "Hard bones & pulling muscles", two tiny enlarged tissue samples only: parallel muscle fibres on left and bone matrix/crystals on right, labels "pull" and "resist compression"; leave central entire region blank for a separate interactive arm. BOTTOM LEFT: heading "Vibration into signals", ear cutaway small at left, large cochlear sensory tissue enlargement right with anchored pink hair cells, purple overlying membrane, golden nerve below. Short labels "moving tissue", "bending hairs", "nerve signals", fine locator line. BOTTOM RIGHT: heading "Breaking down a meal", small digestive tract locator at left and three located magnifications right: mouth starch chain, stomach folded protein, small intestine fat droplets. Tiny labels "mouth", "stomach", "small intestine"; do not include floating food/game pieces. The illustration panels should use only the top 400 pixels of each 1024 square. Plenty of white space and clear restrained typographic hierarchy. NO boxes, no cards, no numbered diagrams, no UI. Exact square panel division matters for mechanical extraction.
